top.title: Blue Origin announces 3rd stage for its powerful New Glenn rocket —and a new engine
top.description: null Blue Origin's big rocket is getting a little bigger. Jeff Bezos' company announced today (Nov. 5) that it has developed a third stage for its New Glenn rocket, which it says will make the powerful launcher more capable and flexible. The stage, called the GS3, "enhances New Glenn's capabilities," Blue Origin said in a blog post today . "The third stage enables direct deployment of satellite constellations to GEO [ geostationary orbit ] and supports heavy-lift science and exploration missions to the moon and deep space." Illustration of the variants of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, with the new GS3 third stage now in the mix. (Image credit: Blue Origin) New Glenn is a two-stage vehicle at the moment. Its reusable first stage is powered by seven of Blue Origin's BE-4 engines, and its second stage features two of the company's BE-3Us. The rocket stands 322 feet (98 meters) tall and can haul 14.3 tons (13 metric tons) to geostationary transfer orbit (GTO) and 50 tons (45 metric tons) to low Earth orbit (LEO). These are the specs for the standard, or "7x2," version of New Glenn. Last year, Blue Origin announced that it's developing a super-heavy variant known as the 9x4, because it will feature nine first-stage BE-4s and four upper-stage BE-3Us. The 9x4 will be nearly 400 feet (122 m) tall, and it will be able to loft 15.4 tons (14 metric tons) to GTO and 77 tons (70 metric tons) to LEO, according to Blue Origin . New Glenn has flown three times to date, each time in the 7x2 configuration. The rocket debuted in January 2025 , then launched again in November 2025 and again on April 19 of this year . Things didn't go according to plan on that latest mission. The rocket deployed AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 communications satellite into the wrong orbit , and the spacecraft ended up being lost. Another setback came just a month later: On May 28, New Glenn exploded on the pad during a routine engine test at Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Station . Blue Origin has been working ever since to rebuild the pad and get New Glenn ready for its fourth flight, which is expected to occur late this year. Blue Origin tests a tank for the GS3 third stage of its New Glenn rocket at its Launch Site One in Texas. (Image credit: Blue Origin) We now know that Blue Origin has also been working on the GS3 while those repairs were underway. The new stage will be powered by one BE-7 engine, which the company developed for use on its Blue Moon spacecraft, one of the two private vehicles that NASA selected to be crewed lunar landers for its Artemis program . (The other is SpaceX's Starship .) Blue Moon landing missions won't need to launch on GS3-equipped New Glenn rockets, according to Blue Origin. But the third stage "can support sustained operations around the moon," the company wrote in today's blog post. top.title: 'What I have learnt is that I should not think so much ahead': Prithvi Shaw prefers to stay in the present
top.description: KOLKATA: Prithvi Shaw showed glimpses of his vintage best as he led Maharashtra to a 10-wicket victory against Bengal in the Ranji Trophy Elite Group ‘C’ match at the Eden Gardens here on Thursday. The opener got his second half-century in this Ranji season to stay unbeaten on 53 off 50 balls while striking three fours and four sixes during his innings. However, Shaw preferred not to look too far ahead but stay in the present. “What I have learnt from experience is that I should not think so much ahead,” he said. “Like I am giving an interview now. After this, I will go to the room and then think about what to do. I don’t think more than that. Just keep winning games. Have good training. Eat well,” he said, laying down his programme. The 26-year-old last played for India five years ago and would definitely look to make a return to the national side. “There is always that thought at the back of the mind. But now I do not think so much ahead,” he explained. His immediate challenge is to put together a consistent run of scores in domestic cricket. The explosive opener has hit two half-centuries in seven innings this Ranji season, with his highest score of 70 coming against Delhi in Maharashtra’s opening match. Since then, he has scored 7, 21, 0, 17 and 12. “Some innings will go bad and some will go well. There is no problem with my start. Big runs are just a matter of one innings,” he felt. Shaw is enjoying leading Maharashtra after shifting from Mumbai last season. “I feel Mumbai and Pune are not too far apart. There is a difference of 1.5 to 2 hours, and I know a lot of players. Ritu (Gaikwad), Ankit (Bawne) here. So I never felt that I have come far from home. I am very comfortable, and have enjoyed it a lot,” he said. The opener enjoyed facing experienced pacer Mohammed Shami. “Shami Bhai is bowling as he used to. There is no change. He is bowling fast. It was about how to play Shami Bhai well because I feel he is the main bowler for such wickets,” he said.

top.title: Glendale's Joelle Rover shows maturity beyond his years after viral moment seen by millions
top.description: SPRINGFIELD — The country was introduced to the Southside Showdown on Oct. 8. Glendale defeated Kickapoo 35-6, but the game was never the story. Glendale wide receiver Joelle Rover was grabbed by referee Kevin Elmer following a touchdown. Millions saw the incident on social media. Influential accounts, including former NFL quarterback and Heisman Trophy winner Robert Griffin III, shared the video. “It’s just like football. Bad plays happen, bad stuff happens,” Rover said. “You just need to move on from it and go to the next play, next opportunity. From that instance, a lot of opportunities have opened up to me.” While MSHSAA has suspended Elmer, Rover’s reaction and maturity were the most striking. Rover never complained and didn’t react negatively in the moment. He said he’s quite proud of it, telling the News-Leader last week. High school football: MSHSAA suspends referee after incident in Glendale game “I can’t say that I’m grateful for what happened,” Rover said. “But I’m grateful for how I acted in the situation.” Rover hasn’t received an apology or been in contact with Elmer. But other Missouri high school referees have sent him messages of support. “They’ve congratulated me on my character. I really appreciated that,” Rover said. “It’s a thing that they didn’t have to and they did it anyways. I’m grateful for that.” During Glendale’s win over Rolla, Rover jogged back to the line of scrimmage to start a new play. A Rolla player was overheard asking him about the referee incident, saying he'd seen the video on TikTok. Rover took it in stride and kept playing. After millions of people know who Rover is, it would be easy for him to succumb to the pressure and not perform. Instead, the wide receiver and defensive back has risen to the challenge. High school football: How Trevor Heman has become one of Missouri's all-time great wide receivers The senior has 727 receiving yards and a team-high 13 touchdowns. His composure and willingness to do anything for the team despite the incident have made head coach Frank Tristan really proud. “Joelle hasn’t changed. He’s a happy-go-lucky, consistent guy,” Tristan said. “The way he has handled this hasn’t surprised me at all. It’s probably why he is a phenomenal three-sport athlete. In some games, the stands will be just screaming at him and he will just keep playing.” Rover and Glendale have a big district semifinal game on the road against Helias Catholic on Friday, Nov. 6. Liam Keating covers high school sports and Missouri State athletics for The Springfield News-Leader. top.title: Colby Covington killed his RAF aura with embarrassing loss to Raul Rosas Jr. — ‘He’s supposed to beat Khamzat?’
top.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - DECEMBER 16: Colby Covington of the United States enters the octagon for a welterweight title fight against Leon Edwards of England during the UFC 296: Edwards vs. Covington event at T-Mobile Arena on December 16, 2023 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Colby Covington provides a great argument for exclusive contracts. “Chaos” is scheduled to wrestle former UFC middleweight champion Khamzat Chimaev atop the RAF Abu Dhabi fight card later this month in UAE, a matchup that had a certain amount of intrigue after Covington dominated Arman Tsarukyan at RAF 11 back in July. Then Covington went and got submitted by UFC bantamweight prospect Raul Rosas Jr. at Hype Italy less than two weeks before his Chimaev showdown, which pretty much killed his aura and left longtime critics ( like this former champion ) laughing their asses off. “He gets f*cking taken down, double-legged, this is the whole fight, 40 seconds,” retired UFC bantamweight and current RAF headliner Henry Cejudo said on his Pound 4 Pound podcast with Kamaru Usman. “Look at this motherf*cker, and he’s supposed to beat Khamzat Chimaev next f*cking week? Colby Covington, you ain’t the king of sh*t no more. This does hurt. I guess people will get over it. If he’s able to come out and beat Khamzat Chimaev, people will forget it, or maybe he’ll get a rematch with Raul Rosas, but I think Raul will probably do that shit again to him.” Covington is currently ranked No. 1 in the promotion . “First and foremost, I would say this: That’s not excusable because of your name and the brand that you’ve built,” Usman added. “It’s not excusable. Now us, real fighters and competitors, we know how difficult and how different they are. Super different. Wrestling and jiu-jitsu are completely different. So Raul Rosas caught him off guard, got in there, and put him away. You could see [Covington’s] face. He was not ready for that level of intensity right away. For a guy that’s supposed to be intense, he was not ready for that level of intensity.” Time for the “king” to surrender his crown?

top.title: Ole Miss and the College Football Playoff roadmap
top.description: BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA - SEPTEMBER 05: A detailed view of the CFP logo on a Clemson equipment case during the second half of a game at Tiger Stadium on September 05, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Tyler Kaufman/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we know by now, our Ole Miss Rebels have debuted at No. 10 in the initial College Football Playoff rankings. Last season was the only year the Rebels have made the playoffs and they debuted at No. 6 and never dropped below No. 7. Some important things to note as we explore the path for Ole Miss is the one and two loss teams they are ahead of and the two loss teams they are behind. Alabama and Texas are ahead of Ole Miss with two losses of their own. Texas has the head-to-head victory while Bama was one of the more puzzling placements. The tide have a home loss to Georgia and an ugly road loss against Tennessee. Texas has a really bad loss to Oklahoma and a home loss to Florida. The Rebels have the blowout road loss (with context) to Florida and a road loss, with injuries, to Texas. So Ole Miss is the only one not to lose at home of the three. What is important to note is that a 7-1 BYU team is only one spot ahead and 8-0 UCLA is just two spots ahead. One loss by either of those schools will mean a lot. The standings directly behind the Rebels looks like this: 11. Notre Dame (7-1) 12. Ohio State (6-2) 13. Tennessee (6-2) 14. LSU (6-2) 15. Texas Tech (7-1) 16. Wake Forest (7-1) 17. Houston (6-2) 18. Missouri (6-2) The CFP Roadmap Route 1: Pretty straight forward, win out and win the SEC Championship and likely receive a bye. Route 2: Win out but not be in the SEC title game (Texas vs Bama), and host a first round game. Route 3: Lose to anyone not named Georgia and all hope is gone. Route 4: “Quality loss” to Georgia. So don’t get blown out. This is where we will spend the time looking at how a loss to Georgia isn’t the end: Georgia finishes 11-1 and wins the SEC Championship. (Still have to play Mizzou and South Carolina). Kentucky loses two more games, preferably to Louisville and Florida. Also have Tennessee and Missouri remaining. UCLA dropping two games. They have to travel to Minnesota and Michigan while hosting Illinois and USC. BYU loses to Utah Notre Dame loses to Miami Florida wins out Tennessee to beat LSU but lose to Texas A&M LSU beats Bama but loses to Tennessee Missouri is a wild card in all of this because of their potential to rack up some big resume wins. They play Texas, Georgia, Kentucky and Oklahoma. Their next three games are against current top 7 teams. If they win two of those and beat Oklahoma, the head-to-head may be the only thing saving Ole Miss at that point, especially since it was dominant. I am not saying all of these things MUST happen, but if we happen to drop the Georgia game, these things would go a long way to keeping hope alive!

top.title: Warriors Withhold $20 Million From Porzingis In Ugly Saga
top.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The New York Knicks are facing a complex situation involving Kristaps Porzingis. The Golden State Warriors have stopped sending money to Porzingis. They say he is not playing, so he does not get his $20 million salary. NBA insider Shams Charania reported this on Tuesday. The move makes an already ugly situation much worse for the big man. He is dealing with a mystery illness and might quit the league for good. New York fans can only watch this drama unfold from the other side of the country. The Cost of an Empty Roster Spot The Warriors are holding back cash and trying to dump the contract, leaving the Knicks to navigate the fallout. Charania noted that the team can move his deal before the Feb. 11 deadline. They want a rival to take on the salary so they can save money. “Absorbing Porzingis’ near-expiring deal would allow a rival team to move a salary out and save money and clear a roster spot via a buyout,” he continued, according to the New York Post . No one wants a player who might retire and costs that much. The Knicks do not need this headache, but the league might have to swallow it. Steve Kerr’s Close Call in New York While Porzingis fights for his paycheck, Steve Kerr is looking back at a chance to coach in New York. Kevin Durant confirmed that Kerr almost took the job years ago. The Knicks had a deal on the table when Phil Jackson was running the show. Kerr stayed in California for his family. He told NBA.com that turning down Phil was hard. “Ultimately, it was agonizing to say no to Phil because of what I think of him and what he’s done for my career,” Kerr said, according to Yardbarker . He knew the job would be a huge challenge far from home. A Young Prospect Gets Cut Meanwhile, the Knicks made their own tough choice on Monday. The team decided not to pick up the option for Pacome Dadiet. Not picking up the option for Pacome Dadiet saves $5.4 million for the 2027-28 season. Dadiet is a 21-year-old from France who has played very little. He only appeared in one game so far this season. The Knicks declined the option, and he will be a free agent soon. This move clears a spot for someone who can actually play. It shows the front office is willing to cut ties when the results do not match the draft pick.

top.title: Duran a Silver Slugger finalist
top.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - SEPTEMBER 25: Ezequiel Duran #20 of the Texas Rangers bats during the game between the Texas Rangers and the Minnesota Twins at Target Field on Friday, September 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Michael Turner/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Texas Rangers jack of all trades Ezequiel Duran is a finalist for the Silver Slugger Award for utility players, it was announced today. Duran is up against the Tigers’ Kevin McGonigle and Sam Antonacci of the White Sox. Duran, who already won the Gold Glove for the utility player spot this offseason, slashed .260/.320/.419 this season, good for a 114 OPS+, and also was 12 for 16 on stolen base attempts. He played all over the diamond for the Rangers, with 49 starts at shortstop, 41 starts at third base, 20 starts in the outfield, 25 starts at second base, and one start at first base. McGonigle, who made his major league debut this season, led American League position players in bWAR this year at 7.1 bWAR. He split his time roughly evenly between shortstop and third base, and slashed .278/.376/.430, good for a 126 OPS+. Antonacci is a rather baffling finalist here. He started 109 games this season in left field and 13 games at second base, although he did appear in another 19 games at second base that he didn’t start. Still, he seems like a left fielder who occasionally played second base rather than a utility guy. He slashed .277/.370/.396, good for a 116 OPS+. Moving forward without Brown III will certainly make things even more difficult against a solid Oklahoma defense. Both Oklahoma and Florida have been capable of big things this year, most notably both knocking off the Texas Longhorns, but they’ve also dealt with rampant inconsistency, so it will be fascinating to see which version of each team shows up for this matchup on Saturday. top.title: Everton Eye £35m Defender: Should Moyes Trigger His Clause?
top.description: Everton Eye £35m Defender: Should Moyes Trigger His Clause? Everton have given themselves a promising platform under David Moyes, sitting seventh in the Premier League after nine matches with 13 points. Three wins, four draws and two defeats have kept the Toffees firmly in the European conversation, while consecutive victories against Newcastle United have strengthened their momentum, including an EFL Cup quarter-final place. Sustaining that progress will require more defensive depth, particularly with several players carrying important responsibilities. Ainsley Maitland-Niles, signed during the summer to provide experienced defensive cover, has established himself as a prominent right-back option and remains contracted until June 2029. Jake O’Brien offers another alternative through 2028, while Jarrad Branthwaite and James Tarkowski have deals running until 2030. Michael Keane, however, reaches the end of his contract in June 2027. Keane’s situation gives Everton another reason to consider defensive succession planning. Moyes values defenders who maintain physical intensity, protect their positions and adjust between a conventional back four and a three-man defence. A younger player with those qualities could reduce the pressure on experienced starters without disrupting the current structure. Sport Witness reports that Everton, Newcastle United and Fulham enquired about Celta Vigo defender Javi Rodríguez in August, with Bournemouth joining the competition. The 23-year-old Spaniard offers precisely the versatility Moyes appreciates, operating at right-back or on the right of a defensive trio. Rodríguez has recorded three goals and one assist across his first 10 competitive appearances in 2026/27, adding attacking contribution to his defensive responsibilities. Yet Celta Vigo have secured him until June 2030 and insist they won’t sell key players in January. His £35m release clause represents the only straightforward route to forcing a departure, while Rodríguez himself has described Celta as the club of his life. Should Everton trigger Rodríguez’s £35m clause in January? VIGO, SPAIN – APRIL 16: Javi Rodriguez of RC Celta Vigo controls the ball during the UEFA Europa League 2025/26 Quarter-Final Leg Two match between Real Club Celta and SC Freiburg at Estadio Balaidos on April 16, 2026 in Vigo, Spain. (Photo by Diogo Cardoso/Getty Images) Everton should resist that temptation. Rodríguez’s versatility and technical composure make him an attractive long-term option, particularly with Keane’s contract approaching its final months. Still, paying £35m upfront for a player who wants to remain in Spain would create unnecessary financial pressure under the Squad Cost Ratio rules. The Friedkin Group must protect the progress Moyes has achieved, rather than compromise squad stability for an expensive January gamble. Maitland-Niles and Tarkowski can cover the immediate requirements, allowing Everton to revisit Rodríguez during summer negotiations.

nigeria.title: Italian chef sacked for refusing to put pineapple on pizza, says it insulted his culture
nigeria.description: An Italian chef in Australia has lost an unfair dismissal claim after being sacked for, among other workplace issues, refusing to serve ham and pineapple pizza, describing the topping as an insult to his culture. Davide Tamburella was dismissed from the now-closed La Costa restaurant in Brisbane in May, following a meeting with management over several complaints about his conduct. One of the issues raised was his refusal to prepare ham and pineapple pizzas for guests attending an event at the restaurant. According to a ruling by Australia’s Fair Work Commission, Tamburella argued that instructions from management “need not be followed when it is offensive to his culture”. The commission noted that the chef’s objection to the fruit was because “he considers, as an Italian, that putting pineapple on a pizza is an insult to his culture”. It also found that this was not the first time he had refused to use pineapple on pizzas, recording three such instances over four years. On a previous occasion, Tamburella had asked his employer to “check how important it is for Italians not to put pineapple on a pizza”. Beyond the dispute over pizza toppings, management raised concerns about his use of foul language, communication style and what it described as an “escalation of frustration in the workplace”. The ruling also detailed an incident in April when Tamburella fractured bones in his right hand after striking a metal handrail at work. The chef had reportedly hoped to secure employer sponsorship for a visa that would allow him to remain in Australia as a permanent resident. However, following his dismissal, the restaurant discontinued the sponsorship process. Tamburella subsequently approached the Fair Work Commission, challenging his dismissal. However, the commission rejected his unfair dismissal claim because it was lodged outside the permitted timeframe. The restaurant’s managing director, Elliot Ingram, told the Daily Mail there was “more to this story than a pizza topping”. The BBC said it had contacted Tamburella for comment. On his LinkedIn profile, the chef describes himself as someone whose career has focused on “delivering exceptional food” and “improving business performance”. He also shared a post titled “letter for chefs” three months ago, centred on the theme of “respecting the ingredients”. His LinkedIn profile indicates that he now works at another restaurant in Brisbane. A BBC check found that pineapple is not included on its menu. Meanwhile, Queensland, where the restaurant was located, is regarded as Australia’s pineapple heartland and produces the country’s commercially grown pineapples. The state is also home to the Big Pineapple, a 16-metre fibreglass structure on the Sunshine Coast that has become a popular local landmark. nigeria.title: 2027 UTME: JAMB moves to shut down substandard CBT centres
nigeria.description: By Joseph Erunke The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) has moved to tighten its grip on the conduct of the 2027 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME), warning that computer-based test (CBT) centres that fail to meet its prescribed standards will be denied accreditation. The Board said only centres with adequate facilities, reliable infrastructure and the operational capacity to guarantee a credible and hitch-free examination would be approved to host candidates in the 2027 exercise. JAMB Registrar, Prof. Segun Aina, gave the indication during a meeting with the leadership of the Chief External Examiners, where preparations and readiness for the accreditation exercise ahead of the 2027 UTME were reviewed. According to a post on the Board’s official X handle on Thursday, the meeting was part of efforts to strengthen examination administration and ensure strict compliance with established operational standards. The Board said the accreditation exercise would serve as a critical screening mechanism to prevent inadequately equipped centres from participating in the examination, thereby protecting candidates from avoidable disruptions and compromising examination conditions. Reiterating its position, JAMB declared that accreditation would not be automatic for CBT centres seeking to participate in the exercise. “Only centres that meet JAMB’s standards will be accredited to host the examination. For candidates, that means a fair and secure place to sit the UTME, wherever they write it,” the Board stated. The development signals JAMB’s determination to strengthen the credibility of the UTME by ensuring that candidates, irrespective of their examination locations, have access to a secure, reliable and conducive testing environment. The strict accreditation regime is also expected to address operational shortcomings that have historically threatened the smooth conduct of computer-based examinations, including inadequate facilities and poor technical readiness. With preparations for the 2027 UTME gathering momentum, the Board maintained that compliance with its accreditation requirements would remain non-negotiable for all CBT centres seeking approval to participate in the nationwide examination. She also expressed gratitude to REST, a charity that supports families dealing with the sudden or tragic deaths of loved ones abroad. Tributes have also poured in from friends and well-wishers, who remembered Chadwick as a kind, caring and cheerful woman. Gombe said the judgment reinforced the principle that leadership positions in political parties must emerge through lawful and constitutionally recognised procedures, not imposition or political expediency, insisting that courts must intervene when parties disregard their own rules. In a statement reacting to the judgment in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, involving him, the ADC and four others, Gombe commended the trial judge for what he described as an independent, impartial and courageous handling of the politically sensitive dispute. “With profound respect for the Bench, and with a deep sense of duty to the administration of justice in Nigeria, I most respectfully commend the Federal High Court and the trial Judge for the independent, impartial, and intellectually rigorous manner in which His Lordship handled and determined the above-referenced matter,” he said. Describing the case as a major test of judicial independence, Gombe said it raised critical questions about party autonomy, internal democracy, constitutional supremacy and the regulatory responsibilities of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). “By subjecting the question of leadership emergence to constitutional and statutory scrutiny, rather than to political expediency, His Lordship affirmed a foundational principle of Nigerian jurisprudence: political parties are not above their own constitutions, and the Electoral Act is not a mere suggestion,” he stated. On the obligation of political parties to obey their internal rules, Gombe said courts had a duty to intervene where established procedures were disregarded. “Where a party’s constitution prescribes a procedure for succession and leadership, that procedure must be obeyed. nigeria.title: Nigerian teenager, Fawaz jailed four years for attempting to steal Porsche in London
nigeria.description: A 19-year-old Nigerian teenager, Fawaz Oyedeji, has been sentenced to four years in prison in the United Kingdom for attempting to steal a £72,500 Porsche Cayenne using an imitation firearm. Oyedeji, who is from Greenwich, London, posed as a prospective buyer after responding to an online advertisement for the luxury sports utility vehicle. He arranged to meet the seller at the victim’s home in Southwark on Tuesday, March 18, to inspect the vehicle. After the victim showed him around the Porsche, the pair entered the front seats to discuss the sale. Oyedeji then produced what appeared to be a firearm, pointed it at the seller and demanded the car keys. However, the victim resisted and fought back, forcing Oyedeji to abandon the attempt and flee from the scene. The police were subsequently alerted and launched an investigation into the incident. Detectives traced the phone used to arrange the vehicle inspection to Oyedeji, establishing that it had been in the vicinity of both his home address and the scene of the attempted robbery. Investigators also obtained CCTV footage showing his movements shortly before and after the incident. Clothing matching what the suspect wore during the attempted robbery was also recovered by officers. Oyedeji was arrested at his home on Leonard Robbins Path within 38 hours of the offence. A jury at the Inner London Crown Court found him guilty after just 26 minutes of deliberation on Wednesday, November 4. He was subsequently sentenced to four years’ imprisonment. nigeria.title: Saudi Arabia executes five Ethiopians for hashish smuggling
nigeria.description: Saudi Arabia has executed five Ethiopian nationals convicted of drug smuggling, bringing the kingdom’s execution toll this year to 205, according to the country’s Interior Ministry. The five were convicted of participating in smuggling hashish into the kingdom, the ministry said in a statement published by the official Saudi Press Agency on Thursday. They were executed in Asir, a province in southwestern Saudi Arabia. The latest executions are the third such announcement involving Ethiopian nationals in recent months. Five Ethiopians were executed on the same day in June, while another five were put to death in July. With the latest executions, 32 Ethiopian nationals have been executed in Saudi Arabia this year, making them the largest foreign national group among those executed. Human Rights Watch warned in July that at least 79 Ethiopians faced an imminent risk of execution over similar drug-related charges. Saudi Arabia recorded 356 executions last year, the highest annual figure in the kingdom’s history. Thousands of Ethiopians work in low-skilled jobs in Saudi Arabia, with many travelling to the oil-rich kingdom through the perilous Eastern Route from the Horn of Africa via Yemen. nigeria.title: France Workers Strike, March For ‘Dignified Wage’
nigeria.description: Striking workers marched across France against the rising cost of living on Thursday, with hundreds of thousands of people expected to take to the streets nationwide in a new escalation following weeks of protest. More than 250,000 people were taking part in demonstrations across 73 cities by the afternoon, the major labour union CGT said. The demonstrations come as the eurozone’s second largest economy battles to redress its finances, six months ahead of elections to replace centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with the far right leading in opinion polls. The high school student movement that began with youths protesting over learning conditions has coincided with widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality, which culminated on October 17 in the worst rioting France has seen in years. Sylvie Larneury, 61, a healthcare manager, and her 61-year-old partner, an IT specialist, were on strike Thursday so they could join the march in the central city of Clermont-Ferrand. “We’re fed up. We’re not starving, but we have to help our children even though they’ve studied,” she said. “We’ve had enough of social injustice,” she added, criticising what she called “a repressive government that defends its own interests and not those of the majority”. The unions are calling for across-the-board wage raises, tax reforms and better learning conditions for young people and have complained about police restrictions on certain protests. As many as 80,000 people were expected to march from 2:00 pm (1300 GMT) in the capital Paris. The planned action prompted the Eiffel Tower to close for the day, operators said on the monument’s website. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Greece Approves 10% Crypto Capital Gains Tax as First Framework Lands Below Draft Rate Greece’s parliament approved on Thursday a bill that imposes a 10% capital gains tax on cryptocurrencies, the first comprehensive legal framework for taxing crypto assets in the country. Cryptocurrency capital gains of up to €500 ($563) a year will be exempt from the new tax, the bill says. For bitcoin holders in Greece, that threshold is a small buffer, not a carve-out for larger positions. “Further implementation directives will be published in the coming weeks, which will also define transparency and audit rules,” a senior finance ministry official told Reuters . An earlier draft circulated in October had floated a 15% rate. The version lawmakers passed lands five points lower, while keeping the €500 annual exemption that was already in that proposal. What the levy covers for bitcoin holders The tax is set to apply from Jan. 1, 2027, Greek coverage of the finance ministry bill says. It is levied on the net gain — the difference between the acquisition price and the transfer price — not on the full sale proceeds. Trading fees and other costs tied to the deal can factor into that calculation. A taxable transfer is not limited to selling for euros. Using cryptocurrency to buy goods or services, or contributing it to cover or increase company capital, can also crystallize a gain under the new rules. That matters for anyone in Greece who pays a merchant in bitcoin rather than converting first. Simply holding bitcoin while its euro value rises does not, by itself, create a tax bill. Crypto-to-crypto swaps, such as bitcoin for another token, are treated as non-taxable events in the explanatory material that accompanied the bill, matching the approach France has used to avoid taxing every hop between coins. Net annual gains at or below €500 are exempt. Losses above €500 in a tax year may be carried forward for up to five years and offset only against future crypto capital gains. Purchases of crypto assets are also being pulled into Greece’s existing “source of funds” checks from 2027, so buyers may need to show that the euros used to acquire bitcoin or other tokens came from declared income or other lawful capital. The rule does not add a separate purchase tax; it widens the audit trail around how coins were funded. Rates on cryptocurrency gains typically run from about 8% to 30% across member states and are usually levied on capital gains, the finance ministry official said. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine South Korea Pushes 22% Crypto Tax to 2029 in Fourth Delay, Offers Three-Year Loss Carryforward South Korea’s government plans to push back its tax on cryptocurrency gains by another two years to 2029, Finance and Economy Minister Lee Hyeong-il said Thursday, in what would be the fourth delay since the levy was written into law. The tax is scheduled to take effect in January. To postpone it, the National Assembly must amend the Income Tax Act before then, and Lee said the government would seek lawmakers’ approval during this year’s regular session. “It weighs heavily on me to propose another delay after the tax has already been postponed three times,” Lee said at a press briefing in Seoul. Korea legislated the tax in 2020 for a 2022 start. It was then pushed to 2023, 2025 and 2027 as officials conceded that tax systems and investor protections were not ready. Waiting on U.S. data The main reason for the new delay is data on overseas trading. When investors move tokens bought abroad onto a Korean exchange, the exchange may have no record of the purchase price needed to calculate a taxable gain. That gap closes in 2029, when Korea and the United States begin exchanging information under the OECD-backed Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, or CARF. Introducing the tax before then could put Korea’s domestic crypto market at a disadvantage, the government said . “Once we begin receiving cryptocurrency transaction data from the United States in 2029, we will have enough information to tax investors who use US exchanges on the same basis as those who trade in the domestic market,” Lee said. The government also cited the need to align the tax with the proposed Digital Asset Act, which would set rules for digital asset businesses and strengthen investor protection. Korea’s broader crypto rulebook has been moving on several fronts , including a Bank of Korea push to write stablecoins into foreign exchange law. Exchanges, investors and lawmakers had pressed for more time, with exchanges saying unclear reporting requirements held up system development and testing. Under current law, only losses from the same year can offset gains, so an investor could owe tax in a profitable year even after losing more the year before. Under the proposal, losses realized in 2029 could offset gains through 2032. Losses realized before the tax takes effect would not be eligible, the government said , citing the volatility of crypto prices as the reason for the change. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. Centered on Africa, the program also looked outward, drawing on solutions from across the Global South and asking how African philanthropy can bridge the divide. The task is to use that small pool to unlock far larger sources, such as pension funds and fixed-income assets, so money reaches businesses that create jobs. sports.title: 'What I have learnt is that I should not think so much ahead': Prithvi Shaw prefers to stay in the present
sports.description: KOLKATA: Prithvi Shaw showed glimpses of his vintage best as he led Maharashtra to a 10-wicket victory against Bengal in the Ranji Trophy Elite Group ‘C’ match at the Eden Gardens here on Thursday. The opener got his second half-century in this Ranji season to stay unbeaten on 53 off 50 balls while striking three fours and four sixes during his innings. However, Shaw preferred not to look too far ahead but stay in the present. “What I have learnt from experience is that I should not think so much ahead,” he said. “Like I am giving an interview now. After this, I will go to the room and then think about what to do. I don’t think more than that. Just keep winning games. Have good training. Eat well,” he said, laying down his programme. The 26-year-old last played for India five years ago and would definitely look to make a return to the national side. “There is always that thought at the back of the mind. But now I do not think so much ahead,” he explained. His immediate challenge is to put together a consistent run of scores in domestic cricket. The explosive opener has hit two half-centuries in seven innings this Ranji season, with his highest score of 70 coming against Delhi in Maharashtra’s opening match. Since then, he has scored 7, 21, 0, 17 and 12. “Some innings will go bad and some will go well. There is no problem with my start. Big runs are just a matter of one innings,” he felt. Shaw is enjoying leading Maharashtra after shifting from Mumbai last season. “I feel Mumbai and Pune are not too far apart. There is a difference of 1.5 to 2 hours, and I know a lot of players. Ritu (Gaikwad), Ankit (Bawne) here. So I never felt that I have come far from home. I am very comfortable, and have enjoyed it a lot,” he said. The opener enjoyed facing experienced pacer Mohammed Shami. “Shami Bhai is bowling as he used to. There is no change. He is bowling fast. It was about how to play Shami Bhai well because I feel he is the main bowler for such wickets,” he said.

sports.title: Glendale's Joelle Rover shows maturity beyond his years after viral moment seen by millions
sports.description: SPRINGFIELD — The country was introduced to the Southside Showdown on Oct. 8. Glendale defeated Kickapoo 35-6, but the game was never the story. Glendale wide receiver Joelle Rover was grabbed by referee Kevin Elmer following a touchdown. Millions saw the incident on social media. Influential accounts, including former NFL quarterback and Heisman Trophy winner Robert Griffin III, shared the video. “It’s just like football. Bad plays happen, bad stuff happens,” Rover said. “You just need to move on from it and go to the next play, next opportunity. From that instance, a lot of opportunities have opened up to me.” While MSHSAA has suspended Elmer, Rover’s reaction and maturity were the most striking. Rover never complained and didn’t react negatively in the moment. He said he’s quite proud of it, telling the News-Leader last week. High school football: MSHSAA suspends referee after incident in Glendale game “I can’t say that I’m grateful for what happened,” Rover said. “But I’m grateful for how I acted in the situation.” Rover hasn’t received an apology or been in contact with Elmer. But other Missouri high school referees have sent him messages of support. “They’ve congratulated me on my character. I really appreciated that,” Rover said. “It’s a thing that they didn’t have to and they did it anyways. I’m grateful for that.” During Glendale’s win over Rolla, Rover jogged back to the line of scrimmage to start a new play. A Rolla player was overheard asking him about the referee incident, saying he'd seen the video on TikTok. Rover took it in stride and kept playing. After millions of people know who Rover is, it would be easy for him to succumb to the pressure and not perform. Instead, the wide receiver and defensive back has risen to the challenge. High school football: How Trevor Heman has become one of Missouri's all-time great wide receivers The senior has 727 receiving yards and a team-high 13 touchdowns. His composure and willingness to do anything for the team despite the incident have made head coach Frank Tristan really proud. “Joelle hasn’t changed. He’s a happy-go-lucky, consistent guy,” Tristan said. “The way he has handled this hasn’t surprised me at all. It’s probably why he is a phenomenal three-sport athlete. In some games, the stands will be just screaming at him and he will just keep playing.” Rover and Glendale have a big district semifinal game on the road against Helias Catholic on Friday, Nov. 6. sports.title: Ole Miss and the College Football Playoff roadmap
sports.description: BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA - SEPTEMBER 05: A detailed view of the CFP logo on a Clemson equipment case during the second half of a game at Tiger Stadium on September 05, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Tyler Kaufman/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we know by now, our Ole Miss Rebels have debuted at No. 10 in the initial College Football Playoff rankings. Last season was the only year the Rebels have made the playoffs and they debuted at No. 6 and never dropped below No. 7. Some important things to note as we explore the path for Ole Miss is the one and two loss teams they are ahead of and the two loss teams they are behind. Alabama and Texas are ahead of Ole Miss with two losses of their own. Texas has the head-to-head victory while Bama was one of the more puzzling placements. The tide have a home loss to Georgia and an ugly road loss against Tennessee. Texas has a really bad loss to Oklahoma and a home loss to Florida. The Rebels have the blowout road loss (with context) to Florida and a road loss, with injuries, to Texas. So Ole Miss is the only one not to lose at home of the three. What is important to note is that a 7-1 BYU team is only one spot ahead and 8-0 UCLA is just two spots ahead. One loss by either of those schools will mean a lot. Missouri (6-2) The CFP Roadmap Route 1: Pretty straight forward, win out and win the SEC Championship and likely receive a bye. Route 2: Win out but not be in the SEC title game (Texas vs Bama), and host a first round game. Route 3: Lose to anyone not named Georgia and all hope is gone. Route 4: “Quality loss” to Georgia. So don’t get blown out. This is where we will spend the time looking at how a loss to Georgia isn’t the end: Georgia finishes 11-1 and wins the SEC Championship. (Still have to play Mizzou and South Carolina). Kentucky loses two more games, preferably to Louisville and Florida. Also have Tennessee and Missouri remaining. UCLA dropping two games. They have to travel to Minnesota and Michigan while hosting Illinois and USC. BYU loses to Utah Notre Dame loses to Miami Florida wins out Tennessee to beat LSU but lose to Texas A&M LSU beats Bama but loses to Tennessee Missouri is a wild card in all of this because of their potential to rack up some big resume wins. They play Texas, Georgia, Kentucky and Oklahoma. Their next three games are against current top 7 teams. If they win two of those and beat Oklahoma, the head-to-head may be the only thing saving Ole Miss at that point, especially since it was dominant. I am not saying all of these things MUST happen, but if we happen to drop the Georgia game, these things would go a long way to keeping hope alive!

sports.title: Warriors Withhold $20 Million From Porzingis In Ugly Saga
sports.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The New York Knicks are facing a complex situation involving Kristaps Porzingis. The Golden State Warriors have stopped sending money to Porzingis. They say he is not playing, so he does not get his $20 million salary. NBA insider Shams Charania reported this on Tuesday. The move makes an already ugly situation much worse for the big man. He is dealing with a mystery illness and might quit the league for good. New York fans can only watch this drama unfold from the other side of the country. The Cost of an Empty Roster Spot The Warriors are holding back cash and trying to dump the contract, leaving the Knicks to navigate the fallout. Charania noted that the team can move his deal before the Feb. 11 deadline. They want a rival to take on the salary so they can save money. “Absorbing Porzingis’ near-expiring deal would allow a rival team to move a salary out and save money and clear a roster spot via a buyout,” he continued, according to the New York Post . No one wants a player who might retire and costs that much. The Knicks do not need this headache, but the league might have to swallow it. Steve Kerr’s Close Call in New York While Porzingis fights for his paycheck, Steve Kerr is looking back at a chance to coach in New York. Kevin Durant confirmed that Kerr almost took the job years ago. The Knicks had a deal on the table when Phil Jackson was running the show. Kerr stayed in California for his family. He told NBA.com that turning down Phil was hard. “Ultimately, it was agonizing to say no to Phil because of what I think of him and what he’s done for my career,” Kerr said, according to Yardbarker . He knew the job would be a huge challenge far from home. A Young Prospect Gets Cut Meanwhile, the Knicks made their own tough choice on Monday. The team decided not to pick up the option for Pacome Dadiet. Not picking up the option for Pacome Dadiet saves $5.4 million for the 2027-28 season. Dadiet is a 21-year-old from France who has played very little. He only appeared in one game so far this season. The Knicks declined the option, and he will be a free agent soon. This move clears a spot for someone who can actually play. It shows the front office is willing to cut ties when the results do not match the draft pick.

sports.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - SEPTEMBER 25: Ezequiel Duran #20 of the Texas Rangers bats during the game between the Texas Rangers and the Minnesota Twins at Target Field on Friday, September 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Michael Turner/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Texas Rangers jack of all trades Ezequiel Duran is a finalist for the Silver Slugger Award for utility players, it was announced today. Duran is up against the Tigers’ Kevin McGonigle and Sam Antonacci of the White Sox. Duran, who already won the Gold Glove for the utility player spot this offseason, slashed .260/.320/.419 this season, good for a 114 OPS+, and also was 12 for 16 on stolen base attempts. He played all over the diamond for the Rangers, with 49 starts at shortstop, 41 starts at third base, 20 starts in the outfield, 25 starts at second base, and one start at first base. McGonigle, who made his major league debut this season, led American League position players in bWAR this year at 7.1 bWAR. He split his time roughly evenly between shortstop and third base, and slashed .278/.376/.430, good for a 126 OPS+. Antonacci is a rather baffling finalist here. He started 109 games this season in left field and 13 games at second base, although he did appear in another 19 games at second base that he didn’t start. Still, he seems like a left fielder who occasionally played second base rather than a utility guy. He slashed .277/.370/.396, good for a 116 OPS+. sports.title: Everton Eye £35m Defender: Should Moyes Trigger His Clause?
sports.description: Everton Eye £35m Defender: Should Moyes Trigger His Clause? Everton have given themselves a promising platform under David Moyes, sitting seventh in the Premier League after nine matches with 13 points. Three wins, four draws and two defeats have kept the Toffees firmly in the European conversation, while consecutive victories against Newcastle United have strengthened their momentum, including an EFL Cup quarter-final place. Sustaining that progress will require more defensive depth, particularly with several players carrying important responsibilities. Ainsley Maitland-Niles, signed during the summer to provide experienced defensive cover, has established himself as a prominent right-back option and remains contracted until June 2029. Jake O’Brien offers another alternative through 2028, while Jarrad Branthwaite and James Tarkowski have deals running until 2030. Michael Keane, however, reaches the end of his contract in June 2027. Keane’s situation gives Everton another reason to consider defensive succession planning. Moyes values defenders who maintain physical intensity, protect their positions and adjust between a conventional back four and a three-man defence. A younger player with those qualities could reduce the pressure on experienced starters without disrupting the current structure. Sport Witness reports that Everton, Newcastle United and Fulham enquired about Celta Vigo defender Javi Rodríguez in August, with Bournemouth joining the competition. The 23-year-old Spaniard offers precisely the versatility Moyes appreciates, operating at right-back or on the right of a defensive trio. Rodríguez has recorded three goals and one assist across his first 10 competitive appearances in 2026/27, adding attacking contribution to his defensive responsibilities. Yet Celta Vigo have secured him until June 2030 and insist they won’t sell key players in January. His £35m release clause represents the only straightforward route to forcing a departure, while Rodríguez himself has described Celta as the club of his life. Should Everton trigger Rodríguez’s £35m clause in January? VIGO, SPAIN – APRIL 16: Javi Rodriguez of RC Celta Vigo controls the ball during the UEFA Europa League 2025/26 Quarter-Final Leg Two match between Real Club Celta and SC Freiburg at Estadio Balaidos on April 16, 2026 in Vigo, Spain. (Photo by Diogo Cardoso/Getty Images) Everton should resist that temptation. Rodríguez’s versatility and technical composure make him an attractive long-term option, particularly with Keane’s contract approaching its final months. Still, paying £35m upfront for a player who wants to remain in Spain would create unnecessary financial pressure under the Squad Cost Ratio rules. The Friedkin Group must protect the progress Moyes has achieved, rather than compromise squad stability for an expensive January gamble. Maitland-Niles and Tarkowski can cover the immediate requirements, allowing Everton to revisit Rodríguez during summer negotiations.

sports.title: Max Verstappen responds to Toto Wolff’s claim that era of "ruthless" F1 drivers is over
sports.description: Motorsport photo Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen has responded to Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff's claim that the era of the "ruthless" F1 driver is over. After Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli clinched his maiden world championship at the Mexican Grand Prix last weekend, Wolff used the 20-year-old as an example of a new kind of champion. "This notion of win at all costs, selfish, opportunistic, ruthless for your own benefit, that model of racing driver has died," Wolff said. "We have a new champion that represents values like humility, like integrity, loyalty, respect, being himself. Should be a role model for many other young drivers in junior formulas. And should be a role model for the few entitled ones in Formula 1, the endless moaners on the radio, the ones that complain, the ones that crash." Wolff did not name any drivers, but Verstappen and two-time champion Fernando Alonso were asked for their views during the drivers' press conference at Interlagos. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing "I mean, everyone is entitled to their opinion, right? I have nothing else to say, really," Verstappen said. "Every person is different anyway. I think that’s what is good for Formula 1, because if everyone has the same personality, it’s very boring." Alonso was invited to share his thoughts on Wolff's comments, but he refused. Verstappen was more expansive when the subject turned to his own radio messages, which have often featured complaints about the car this season. "With shifts or whatever that you hear me complain about, it’s just because I’m never satisfied, because I think always certain things can be better, and I always try to fine-tune or find improvements," the Dutchman explained. "So if you hear it as complaining or whatever, it’s more for me to make sure that the team is always looking into details to try and find more lap time because I know there is more lap time in it." technology.title: Software squeezes more data out of Webb Telescope for imaging exoplanets
technology.description: With a huge and still-growing catalog of exoplanets, researchers are anxious to take the next steps: trying to infer what conditions are like on them, either by imaging them directly or by capturing the light that has passed through their atmosphere. Both are substantial challenges, given the presence of stars that are far, far brighter than light that has come to us via the planet. While telescopes can be fitted with devices called coronagraphs that block out much of a star's light, there are limits to their effectiveness, caused by noise from subtle variations in the telescope's configuration and pointing between observations. Now, researchers have developed a new software package that optimizes a physical model of the telescope in a way that allows us to better model these differences, producing low-noise imaging of exoplanets. Point spreads Central to this work is the concept of a point spread function. If you use a telescope to image a single point of light, it will not appear that way in the actual image. Instead, it will be slightly blurry and spread out, due to imperfections in the telescope hardware and the limits of our ability to keep it pointed accurately through the time it takes to image something. The mathematical description of how a telescope distorts a point of light is called its point spread function. Read full article Comments

technology.title: Get root on a musl Linux system by slamming it with an overly long password
technology.description: On certain Linux systems, an attacker could gain root access by entering a password longer than 256 bytes. The vulnerability, dubbed *sshole by Wakefield researcher Özgün Kültekin, who discovered it, can only be exploited in very specific conditions. The flaw affects certain Linux systems using musl libc instead of the traditional GNU C library, and even then only those running OpenSSH's secure shell daemon without Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) and with password authentication enabled. If those conditions are met, and at least one other account has a valid password hash, accounts that shouldn't accept passwords, such as root, key-only deployment users, and LDAP users, may be accessed by supplying a password between 257 and 1,024 characters. The targeted accounts must have an asterisk (*) in their password field, and direct root login remains subject to OpenSSH's configuration. That might seem niche, but sorry: It’s not. Musl libc is common in embedded Linux systems due to its low footprint. More critically than that, it's also the standard C library for Alpine Linux, which provides official cloud images for both AWS and Azure. Some Alpine systems running in those environments may therefore be vulnerable, depending on their configuration. Dawn of the *sshole The vulnerability in OpenSSH on musl-based Linux systems dates back to 2016, but Kültekin explains that its roots go back much further – to the BSD Unix era, actually. In 1980, Sun Microsystems cofounder and BSD Unix heavyweight Bill Joy was involved in the development of BSD Unix, whose password file contained a single asterisk in the /etc/passwd entry for the daemon user. The asterisk wasn't a password hash and effectively disabled password authentication for that account. Nowadays, password hashes typically live in /etc/shadow and contain hashed information that the system uses to verify a plaintext password entered by a user. Asterisks are still present for accounts that aren't supposed to accept password logins, but as Kültekin explains in his writeup, that isn't exactly a foolproof way to keep people out. The crypt() function, which generates password hashes for comparison with stored values, can return NULL if it can't compute a hash. Applications that fail to check that result may crash. Musl libc's developers instead chose to return a single character for certain failures, and they picked the asterisk. Musl also added SHA-512-based password hashing around the same time, which Kültekin notes gets slower the longer a password is, potentially leading to denial of service if someone floods a server with a super-long password. Musl capped passwords at 256 bytes, and you can likely see where this is going. In 2016, OpenSSH introduced a workaround to prevent attackers from enumerating valid account names through SSH. technology.description: While the upcoming Grand Theft Auto VI won't be available on PC this month, some gamers are making ridiculous preparations to use their PC graphics cards to apply Nvidia's DLSS 5 technology to the console exclusive. On an explicitly unmoderated GTAVI subreddit, user RevolutionaryBus8208 lays out a proposed setup, which runs a PlayStation 5 through a 4K capture card to a PC. From there, the video signal is run through Veyra , an open source tool that can apply DLSS 5's AI-powered "neural rendering" to video content. The result—which also uses DLSS frame generation to increase the 30 fps source to a 90 fps output—is then piped back to a 4K TV, theoretically adding some of the benefits of a beefy PC graphics card to a console-exclusive game. To demonstrate the potential of this setup, RevolutionaryBus8208 used Veyra to upscale the Grand Theft Auto VI Extended Look trailer posted in August. The resulting DLSS-ified version looks a bit better in places, with sharper background elements, subtler shadows, and more believable light scattering on some surfaces. science.title: Blue Origin announces 3rd stage for its powerful New Glenn rocket —and a new engine
science.description: null Blue Origin's big rocket is getting a little bigger. Jeff Bezos' company announced today (Nov. 5) that it has developed a third stage for its New Glenn rocket, which it says will make the powerful launcher more capable and flexible. The stage, called the GS3, "enhances New Glenn's capabilities," Blue Origin said in a blog post today . "The third stage enables direct deployment of satellite constellations to GEO [ geostationary orbit ] and supports heavy-lift science and exploration missions to the moon and deep space." Illustration of the variants of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, with the new GS3 third stage now in the mix. (Image credit: Blue Origin) New Glenn is a two-stage vehicle at the moment. Its reusable first stage is powered by seven of Blue Origin's BE-4 engines, and its second stage features two of the company's BE-3Us. The rocket stands 322 feet (98 meters) tall and can haul 14.3 tons (13 metric tons) to geostationary transfer orbit (GTO) and 50 tons (45 metric tons) to low Earth orbit (LEO). These are the specs for the standard, or "7x2," version of New Glenn. Last year, Blue Origin announced that it's developing a super-heavy variant known as the 9x4, because it will feature nine first-stage BE-4s and four upper-stage BE-3Us. The 9x4 will be nearly 400 feet (122 m) tall, and it will be able to loft 15.4 tons (14 metric tons) to GTO and 77 tons (70 metric tons) to LEO, according to Blue Origin . New Glenn has flown three times to date, each time in the 7x2 configuration. The rocket debuted in January 2025 , then launched again in November 2025 and again on April 19 of this year . Things didn't go according to plan on that latest mission. The rocket deployed AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 communications satellite into the wrong orbit , and the spacecraft ended up being lost. Another setback came just a month later: On May 28, New Glenn exploded on the pad during a routine engine test at Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Station . Blue Origin has been working ever since to rebuild the pad and get New Glenn ready for its fourth flight, which is expected to occur late this year. Blue Origin tests a tank for the GS3 third stage of its New Glenn rocket at its Launch Site One in Texas. (Image credit: Blue Origin) We now know that Blue Origin has also been working on the GS3 while those repairs were underway. The new stage will be powered by one BE-7 engine, which the company developed for use on its Blue Moon spacecraft, one of the two private vehicles that NASA selected to be crewed lunar landers for its Artemis program . science.title: The economic benefits of the covid vaccines may be double what we thought
science.description: The covid-19 vaccines were costly to produce, but paid for themselves many times over Paul Christian Gordon / Alamy The covid-19 vaccines may have provided health and economic benefits worth up to $64.3 trillion in the first year alone – almost double an earlier estimate. Previously, researchers calculated that the $79.4 billion invested in developing covid-19 vaccines saw a return of between $4.8 trillion and $37.9 trillion globally in the first 12 months after their rollout. But now, a reanalysis of the data suggests it is actually between $6.43 trillion and $64.3 trillion. This means that for every $1 spent on the vaccines’ development, between $59.70 and $809 was gained in that year. “It is great to finally see this research published to demonstrate the enormous health and financial benefits gained from covid-19 vaccines, in comparison to the costs that went into their development and delivery,” says Hallie Benjamin at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine. Read more Does each new covid-19 variant pose a significant threat? The $6.43 trillion figure is based on a cost-effectiveness analysis that is generally used in the health sector and factors in quality of life, while the $64.3 trillion figure is based on a cost-benefit analysis used in the public sector. Advertisement Both include data from 173 countries on averted hospitalisations, productivity losses and lives saved. For instance, one of the estimates Benjamin and her colleagues used came from modelling that suggested the vaccines prevented 14 million to 20 million deaths in their first year. The initial $4.8 trillion and $37.9 trillion figures were released when the research was in a preprint stage, before it had been peer-reviewed. “We made many changes throughout the peer-review process that strengthened the quality of our findings,” says Benjamin. The researchers originally used the Value of Statistical Life Years, which considers how many years a person would be likely to live because of the vaccine, a figure that would be lower if someone was older. As part of the peer-review process, they were advised to use the Value of Statistical Life. Team member Mark Jit at New York University says this treats life spans more equally and is aligned with recommendations for valuing mortality-risk reductions. Free newsletter Sign up to Health Check Sign up to newsletter The cost-benefit analysis figure also increased significantly due to a change from calculating the economic value of avoiding a death, says Jit. But the returns weren’t equally distributed. The researchers found that the vaccines had the highest returns in richer countries. This was probably because poorer countries accessed them later, so fewer lives were saved and fewer productivity and healthcare costs were averted, says Jit. The results are “a message about the need for being able to distribute the vaccines fairly to the people most in need around the world”, he says. Covid raises risk of heart issues in children

science.title: Tomb in Siberia reveals humans were using cannabis 2800 years ago
science.description: Researchers excavate a burial mound containing horse and human bones along with cannabis seeds Frozen Corpses Golden Treasures, T.Wallace & G. Casp A hair found in a 2800-year-old tomb in Siberia has yielded the earliest definitive evidence of cannabis being used as a psychoactive drug. But the history of such use is likely to go back much further. Genomic studies suggest that the domestication of cannabis plants ( Cannabis sativa ) was happening in China about 12,000 years ago , with people potentially exploiting it for oil and hemp fibre. Archaeological sites with artefacts made from hemp dating to 7500 years ago have been found in China and Japan . The earliest firm evidence of the plant’s use as a drug had been chemical traces on wooden braziers in China that implied humans were “smoking” cannabis 2500 years ago as part of funeral rites. Read more How a surge in ancient plagues 5000 years ago shaped humanity Now, Gino Caspari at the University of Bern in Switzerland and his colleagues have pushed the date back another 300 years with a find at the Tunnug 1 burial mound in the Uyuk Valley of southern Siberia. Advertisement The royal burial mound dates to the time of the Scythians, nomads renowned for their military skills and horseback archery who spread across a huge swathe of Eurasia. In an excavation trench at the centre of the mound, Caspari and his colleagues recovered almost 1000 whole cannabis seeds. Radiocarbon dating indicated that they were deposited around the start of the 8th century BC, some 2800 years ago. He says we can’t say how the person consumed the drug – it might have been smoked or the seeds could have just been ingested.
